title: Tourist Season, 2006
logline: A tourist asks Wood to draw her. He does. It's kind. He's surprised again. The chorus is not.

panels.composition: Gully's. A TOURIST, older, in a sun hat, asking WOOD on the stool. BARNABY. The chorus at the back with a sign: DO IT.

balloons.text: Would you draw me? For my husband. He couldn't come.

image.prompt: an older tourist in a sun hat asking a thin man on a shop stool with a drawing pad, a dog beneath, small stick figures at the back holding a sign, muddy flats

panels.composition: Wood drawing her. Ninety seconds. Looking at her more than the pad.

image.prompt: close-up of a man drawing a portrait quickly while looking more at his subject than at the pad

panels.composition: The drawing: her, the hat, the sun, and — because she said 'he couldn't come' — a second chair beside her, empty, drawn without comment.
props: the drawing with an empty chair

image.prompt: close-up of a quick ink portrait of an older woman in a sun hat with an empty chair drawn beside her

panels.composition: The tourist looking at it. Her face. Wood already looking away. The chorus has put the sign down.

image.prompt: an older woman looking at a portrait with her face changing, a thin man looking away, stick figures at the back with their sign lowered, no words

art.line: brush-pen scanned; muddy digital flats; Sundays in watercolor, improving
art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays gray-green, rust, one warm

notes: The empty chair beside her. Tourist Season stops being cruel and the strip stops pretending it was.
